name: Pediatric volar modified Henry approach to the distal radius
corridor: Through FCR sheath, ulnar to radial artery, then between FPL and radial artery to pronator quadratus

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on a radiolucent hand table, forearm supinated, and wrist freely imageable.

setup.text: Map the physis, FCR, radial artery, and median-nerve branches; plan the least invasive fixation compatible with stable reduction.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark FCR, radial styloid, wrist crease, radial artery pulse, and radiocarpal joint.

incision.text: Incise along the radial border of FCR, tailored to the fracture and implant length.

superficial_interval.text: Open FCR sheath and retract tendon medially while protecting the radial artery laterally and palmar cutaneous median-nerve branch medially.

deep_interval.text: Develop between FPL and radial artery, sweep FPL medially, and elevate pronator quadratus extraperiosteally with an L-shaped incision.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous nerve plane, FCR sheath, FPL-artery interval, pronator quadratus, then distal radius.

structures_encountered.text: FCR, radial artery, palmar cutaneous median-nerve branch, FPL, pronator quadratus, physis, and distal radius are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial artery, median nerve and palmar cutaneous branch, FPL and other flexors, physis, and radiocarpal cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid distal nerve-branch injury and unnecessary transphyseal dissection or fixation; identify the joint and physis fluoroscopically.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid sustained radial-artery or median-nerve traction and protect flexors from sharp retractors.

exposure.text: Exposes the volar distal radius for direct reduction while preserving options for physeal-respecting fixation.

limitations.text: Dorsal, radial-styloid, or ulnar-column fragments may require a separate targeted exposure.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along FCR or add a separate column-specific approach rather than over-retracting neurovascular structures.

indications.text: Use selectively for irreducible, unstable, or displaced pediatric distal-radius fractures requiring open volar control.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid open exposure when stable acceptable closed reduction is achievable or when the key fragment is inaccessible volarly.

implant_implications.text: Use low-profile, maturity-appropriate fixation, minimize physeal violation, and keep screws out of radiocarpal and dorsal tendon compartments.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm physis, joint surface, reduction, implant trajectory, and screw containment on orthogonal and tangential views.

closure.text: Replace pronator quadratus over implants when possible, close FCR sheath without trapping the cutaneous nerve, then close skin.

complications.text: Complications include nerve or artery injury, tendon irritation, physeal arrest, joint penetration, infection, stiffness, and symptomatic hardware.

bailouts.text: Add the needed column-specific exposure when reduction remains unseen and choose alternate fixation if physeal safety cannot be maintained.

procedure_applications.condition: An irreducible or unstable pediatric distal-radius fracture requires direct volar reduction and fixation

questions.question: What is the defining interval?
questions.answer: Between FCR and radial artery, ulnar to the artery.

questions.question: Which nerve branch is vulnerable?
questions.answer: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve.
